item.title: 02 Oct 2026 10:30
item.description:
One of the perks of my job is to meet and work with so many interesting people. And with anything that awesome, it’s almost always short-lived. People move on once their assignment comes to an end and somebody else comes and fills their shoes. Snyder is leaving us this weekend and he will very much be missed!

We have an unsaid practice in ST to host Thirsty Thursday’s. It’s a HUGE morale booster for a bunch of teams and turns out to be great way to get folks together just before the week comes to an end. Snyder was a frequent TT participant and we’ll absolutely miss him.

Made him a miniature representation of TT last night. Took me around 4 hours to get it to this state and I think I’m going to leave this as is and not color it. Coloring is not my artsy forte yet and I think this kinda gives him (or his grandkids) a platform to build-on. Until next, Snyder! 1600 somewhere on TTs. 🔗

item.title: 27 Sep 2026 10:30
item.description:
Over the last few weeks, I’ve been contemplating how exactly I would like to set this Model rail diorama. My primary concern was mobility. I want to be able to dismantle it quickly if needed and pack these all up into two or three big boxes. Ideally I would stage this on a wooden platform, staged on a wall at shoulder height. Wasn’t quite lucky finding the wood I would need for that and then given we only have about 10 months left here, I wasn’t invested enough.

Yesterday morning, It struck me to use the surfboard’s box as a platform. Staged it on the ground in our master bedroom and quickly threw a bedsheet on top of it. Added 6 25cents coins on each compartments underside for stability weight and tested out the connections. The engine rides beautifully, but the compartments still detach randomly. Decided to troubleshoot that later - Will most likely have to add a couple more coins and check the couplers later..

While at it, I reworked the rail platform a bit. I’d previously built a platform using paper mache. That didn’t feel strong enough and was warping a bit. Built another platform using balsa wood and that turned out pretty good. Need to add more stabilizers later. Eventually I want to add more responsive lighting in. Built some tiny benches and then tiny people. I think they’ve turned out pretty neat! Still need to figure out the colors et al. But I think I’ve learnt how to work the wood and the tiny people was a fantastic add-on I’m super proud of!

Here’s what I’ve visualized this whole setup to look like: The rail-line would meander around a large water body via a couple tunnels to make it’s way to the platform. Each side of the platform would have rail lines - ideally with switchover connections. The platform would connect to the station via an overhead walkover bridge. The land around the station and by the rails would all be decked by miniature features you’d find in the country-side. Would be wonderful to add a waterfall, some clouds (that move?) and some neat visual effects.

Each of these tiny miniatures takes several hours and multiple takes. This is turning out to be way more involved than I had imagined, but I’m absolutely loving it. Been a while that something has gotten my attention so much! 🔗
